statements.says: General limitation period is fifteen years, except where a special statute or the listed exceptions apply.
Periodic renewable rights (rent of buildings, arrears, salaries and wages, pensions) are time-barred after five years, even if the debtor acknowledged them.
Exception: revenue owed by a bad-faith possessor or by the manager of undivided property lapses only after fifteen years.
Fees of doctors, pharmacists, lawyers, engineers, experts, bankruptcy agents, brokers, professors and teachers for work and expenses are time-barred after two years.
Taxes and duties owed to the State are time-barred after four years; start dates are given for annual duties and for judicial-paper duties.
The right to claim refund of taxes and duties wrongly paid is time-barred after four years from the day of payment.
These rules do not affect provisions of special statutes.
Introduces the rights time-barred after one year.
Claims of traders and craftsmen for goods supplied to non-traders, and of hotels and restaurants, are time-barred after one year.
Sums owed to workers and other employees for their work are time-barred after one year.
A party relying on the one-year limitation must swear he actually paid; the judge directs the oath of his own motion to heirs or guardians (that they do not know of the debt or know it was paid).
For rights in articles 309 and 311, the period starts when creditors finish rendering their services, even if they go on rendering others.
If a written instrument is drawn up for such a right, it is time-barred only after fifteen years.
A limitation period is counted in days, not hours; the first day is not counted and the period is complete when its last day ends.
Absent a special text, limitation starts only from the day the debt becomes payable.
Examples: conditional debt runs from fulfilment of the condition; eviction warranty from proof of eviction; deferred debt from expiry of the term.
If the date of payment depends on the creditor's will, limitation runs from when he can declare it.
Limitation does not run while a legitimate obstacle prevents the creditor from claiming, nor between principal and representative.
Limitation of up to five years does not run against persons lacking capacity, absentees and persons sentenced to criminal penalties who have no legal representative.
Limitation longer than five years does not run against those persons even if they have a legal representative, for the whole period of incapacity.

Limitation is interrupted by judicial claim (even before an incompetent court), by notice or seizure, by lodging the claim in bankruptcy or distribution, or by any act of the creditor during pleadings to prove his right.
Limitation is interrupted by the debtor's express or implied acknowledgment; leaving a pledged asset with the creditor as security is an implied acknowledgment.
After interruption a new period starts when the effect of the cause of interruption ends, with the same length as the first.

Exception: new period is fifteen years if the debt is adjudged by a final judgment, or if a one-year debt is interrupted by acknowledgment, unless the judgment includes periodic obligations not yet payable at judgment.
Limitation extinguishes the obligation but leaves a natural obligation; accessories lapse with the right even if their own period is incomplete.
The court may not rule limitation of its own motion; it needs a request from the debtor, a creditor of his, or any interested person, even if the debtor does not invoke it.
Limitation may be invoked at any stage of the case, even on appeal.
Limitation cannot be waived before the right to it is acquired, nor may the parties agree on a period different from the legal one.
After limitation is acquired, a person able to dispose of his rights may waive it, even impliedly, but the waiver does not bind creditors if made to their harm.
A plea of inadmissibility aims at declaring the opponent's claim inadmissible for lack of right to sue, including limitation and expiry of a forfeiture period, without examining the merits.
Parties may raise the plea of inadmissibility at any stage, even after pleas on the merits.
The judge must raise inadmissibility of his own motion if it concerns public order, notably non-respect of appeal periods or absence of appeal.
Periods for opposition, appeal, retraction request and cassation are extended by two months for persons residing outside the national territory.
All periods in this code are counted in full; the day of notification (or official notification) and the day the period expires are not counted.
Holidays falling within the period are counted.
Holidays are official feast days and weekly rest days under the rules in force.
If the last day is not wholly or partly a working day, the period is extended to the next working day.

openPoints.question: Wages and sums owed to workers: article 309 gives five years for wages and salaries, article 312 gives one year for sums owed to workers for their work. Which applies to a labour wage claim?
readings: 312 (one year) is the special rule for workers and prevails over 309
309 (five years) applies to periodic wages, 312 to other sums owed to workers
A labour-law text not given here governs

openPoints.question: Does CPCA 405 (day of notification and last day not counted, holidays counted, extension to next working day) govern civil-code limitation periods?
readings: No: 405 says periods 'in this law' (the procedure code), and civil-code 314 governs limitation (first day not counted, period complete at the end of the last day)
Yes by analogy, so that a limitation period ending on a non-working day extends to the next working day

openPoints.question: Does civil-code 314 (counted by days; first day not counted) apply to periods stated in months or years?
readings: Yes: the period is counted by calendar dates from the day after the starting event and ends at the end of the last day
No fixed text: the conversion of years into days is not stated

openPoints.question: Who raises limitation: civil-code 321 forbids the court to rule it of its own motion, while CPCA 67 lists limitation among pleas of inadmissibility and CPCA 69 requires the judge to raise public-order inadmissibility of his own motion.
readings: Limitation is not public order: only a party or interested person raises it (321, the special rule for limitation)
CPCA 67 treats limitation as inadmissibility, so 69 could apply if it is public order; no text given says it is

openPoints.question: Is the period in CPCA 504 (labour claim time limit) a limitation or a forfeiture, and who may raise it?
readings: Text not given: cannot be decided here

openPoints.question: Start of the 1-year, 2-year and 15-year (article 313 para 2) periods: article 313 para 1 names only 309 and 311.
readings: General start of article 315 (day the debt becomes payable)
Completion of services, by extension of 313 para 1

openPoints.question: Is the acknowledgment/interruption by notice (article 317, 'بالتنبيه') satisfied by any formal notice, including a registered letter?
readings: Only formal notice in the legal sense (e.g. by bailiff)
Any notice served on the debtor; the text does not say the means

openPoints.question: How do the slots (notice, defendant abroad, bankruptcy, public servant, work accident) affect periods? Only abroad residence is addressed (404 extends appeal-type periods, not limitation); the others have no text here.
readings: No effect from the texts given
Effects exist in texts not given (labour code, commercial code, public-service statutes)
